title: Dynamic Strings
summary: Building text of any length safely in C - why fixed char arrays run out, a growable string buffer with length and capacity, appending with realloc, a printf-style append with vsnprintf that measures before it writes, handing ownership of the result to the caller, and the common string-building bugs this design prevents.

cards.a:
The length the full output would have

With size 0 nothing is written, but the return value (not counting the terminating zero) tells you how big a buffer to allocate; add 1 for the zero.

cards.q: Why does the capacity double instead of growing by the amount needed?
cards.a:
So reallocations stay rare and appending is O(1) on average

Growing by exactly what is needed copies the whole string on every append, O(n²) in total. Doubling uses some extra memory but copies far less.

cards.q: Why is strcat in a loop slow for long strings?
cards.a:
It searches for the end of the string each time

strcat has to find the terminating zero first, so each append costs the current length; keeping the length yourself avoids the scan.
